scenes.narration: Rule 1. Among two fractions with the same denominator, the one with the greater numerator is the greater of the two. 8 by 9 and 5 by 9 are both ninths. 8 ninths is more, so 8 by 9 is greater than 5 by 9.
scenes.captions: Rule 1. Among two fractions with the same denominator, the one with the greater numerator is the greater of the two. 8/9 and 5/9 are both ninths. 8 ninths is more, so 8/9 > 5/9.

scenes.narration: Rule 2. Among two fractions with the same numerator, the one with the smaller denominator is the greater of the two. Sixths are bigger parts than eighths. So 5 by 6 is greater than 5 by 8.
scenes.captions: Rule 2. Among two fractions with the same numerator, the one with the smaller denominator is the greater of the two. Sixths are bigger parts than eighths. So 5/6 > 5/8.

scenes.narration: When the numerators and denominators are both different, cross multiply. To compare 3 by 8 and 5 by 12: 3 times 12 is 36, and 8 times 5 is 40. 36 is less than 40. Hence, 3 by 8 is less than 5 by 12.
scenes.captions: When the numerators and denominators are both different, cross multiply. To compare 3/8 and 5/12: 3 × 12 = 36, and 8 × 5 = 40. 36 < 40. Hence, 3/8 < 5/12.

scenes.narration: Let us try 5 by 9 and 6 by 11. 5 times 11 is 55, and 9 times 6 is 54. 55 is greater than 54. Hence, 5 by 9 is greater than 6 by 11.
